s1.syndrome_frame: excessive sweating of the buttocks and sacrum with significant impact on daily life
salient_findings: excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previous successful treatment of axillary hyperhidrosis with 20% aluminum chloride
unsuccessful treatment of intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride
key_facts: 31-year-old male nursing student
history of axillary hyperhidrosis
excessive sweating of the buttocks
most severe sweating at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previous treatment with 20% aluminum chloride for axillary hyperhidrosis
unsuccessful treatment of intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride
uses absorbent pads due to severity of the condition
unable to attend work due to the condition
Minor starch-iodine test performed to localize sites of overactive sweating
areas of significant sweating identified in the sacral region and intergluteal cleft

shortlist.label: Intergluteal and sacral hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: matches the patient's symptoms of excessive sweating in the buttocks and sacrum

shortlist.label: Primary focal hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the patient's history of axillary hyperhidrosis and current symptoms

shortlist.label: Idiopathic localized hyperhidrosis
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the patient's localized excessive sweating

shortlist.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
shortlist.why_kept: could be considered due to the patient's symptoms of excessive sweating and potential skin inflammation

shortlist.label: Intertrigo
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms of skin irritation and excessive sweating in the intergluteal cleft

raw.rationale: The patient's history of excessive sweating, particularly in the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, along with the results of the Minor starch-iodine test, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary focal hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: While the patient does have focal hyperhidrosis, the specific locations of the sweating (intergluteal cleft and sacrum) are more precisely described by intergluteal and sacral hyperhidrosis

rejected.label: Idiopathic localized hyperhidrosis
rejected.why: The patient's condition is localized to specific areas, but the term 'idiopathic' implies an unknown cause, whereas the patient's symptoms and test results suggest a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: There is no mention of the patient having the characteristic symptoms of hidradenitis suppurativa, such as painful nodules or abscesses

rejected.label: Intertrigo
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the typical signs of intertrigo, such as erythema, maceration, or satellite lesions
